desc:
Two arrays a and b, both sorted in non-decreasing order, are given. Take one element from each array to form a pair; there are a.length * b.length pairs (pairs at different positions are different even if their values match). Consider all the pair sums a[i] + b[j] in sorted order.

Return the value of the k-th smallest sum (1-indexed). Note that k can be in the millions, so listing the sums is not an option.

a = [1, 7, 11], b = [2, 4, 6], k = 5
sums sorted: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 13, 15, 17
result = 11
constraints: a and b are sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: There can be up to 4 million sums. A heap that pops k times is too slow when k is that big. Think about searching over the value of the answer instead of over the pairs.
For a guess x, can you count how many sums are at most x in O(n + m) using the sorted order? As you move through a upward, the largest usable element of b only moves downward.
Binary search the smallest x whose count is at least k. Counting: pointer j starts at the end of b; for each a[i] in increasing order, decrease j while a[i] + b[j] > x, then add j + 1.
editorial: Let count(x) be the number of pairs with sum at most x. It is non-decreasing in x, and the k-th smallest sum is the smallest x with count(x) ≥ k. So binary search on x between a[0] + b[0] and a[-1] + b[-1]; the range is at most about 4·109, so around 32 iterations.

To compute count(x) with two pointers: process a in increasing order and keep j, the last index of b with a[i] + b[j] ≤ x. As a[i] grows, the allowed b[j] shrinks, so j only moves left. Each a[i] contributes j + 1 pairs. One count takes O(n + m).
Total time is O((n + m) log(range)). The smallest x with count(x) ≥ k is automatically an actual pair sum, since otherwise x - 1 would have the same count.
